Compare two profiles

Source: R/profile_compare.R
profile_compare.Rd

Measures how far each summary of a synthetic profile is from the same summary of a real profile. It judges each distance against the sampling noise of a synthetic table of that size.

Usage

profile_compare(real, synth, margin = 0.05, n_boot = 200L, seed = 1L)

Arguments

real

The csdb_profile of the real data.

synth

The csdb_profile of the synthetic data. Profile the synthetic data with the same columns, k and max_levels as the real data.

margin

The amount by which a distance can exceed the noise of its table and still pass.

n_boot

The number of bootstrap draws for each table.

seed

The seed for set.seed(). The function restores the random state of the caller on exit.

Value

A data.table with the columns column, property, distance, threshold and pass. pass is distance <= threshold. A crosstab or a dependency names its columns as "a,b".

Details

Each row compares one summary of real with the same summary of synth. The tables of counts are levels, days, weeks, months, quarters, bins, crosstab and group_sizes. The distance of two tables is the total variation distance of their shares. Each table is normalised over its own published cells, so suppressed cells take no part.

The function aligns the cells of the two tables first:

  • Ordered cells are days, weeks, months, runs of quarters, bins, ranges of group sizes, and the levels of a number or a time. Cells of the two tables that overlap join one aligned cell. So each aligned cell is a union of whole cells of both tables. It takes the coarser resolution of the two at that place. The last range of group sizes has no end.

  • Unordered cells are the levels of a TEXT or BOOLEAN column and the cells of a crosstab. They align by value.

An aligned cell that only one table holds counts in the distance. Merge suppression drops no ordered row. The simulator draws no row in a cell that real suppressed.

The threshold of a table comes from n_boot draws:

  1. Each draw is a multinomial sample from the real shares. Its size is the size of the synthetic table: its rows, suppressed cells included, or its identifiers for group_sizes.

  2. An ordered draw puts each row at a uniform value within its real cell, as simulate_from_profile() does.

  3. The function applies the k merge of profile_query() to the draw, with the k and max_levels of real. Unordered cells below k are removed.

  4. The threshold is the 95th percentile of the distances of the draws from real, plus margin.

The other rows:

  • missing_share: the absolute difference of the two shares. The draws are binomial, of synth$n_rows rows at the real share. The function skips a column where either share is "suppressed".

  • n_distinct: 0 when the synthetic n_distinct is in the range that synth$n_rows uniform draws from the real n_distinct values can reach. Otherwise the absolute difference from the nearest end of that range, divided by that end. The range runs from the expected number of distinct values in those draws up to the smaller of the real n_distinct and synth$n_rows. Both ends are rounded down to a multiple of the k of synth, as the profile rounds n_distinct. The threshold is margin.

  • dependency: 0 when both profiles agree on holds, otherwise 1. The threshold is 0.

A summary of real that synth lacks, or holds in a form that does not align, gets distance 1 and threshold margin. A schema_only column has only its missing_share compared. The draws do not model the noise that noise adds to a profile.

See also

Other simulation functions: profile_schema(), simulate_from_profile()

Examples

d <- data.frame(sex = rep(c("female", "male"), 500))
p <- profile_data(d, c(sex = "TEXT"), columns = c(sex = "full"))
sim <- simulate_from_profile(p, n = 1000)
s <- profile_data(sim, c(sex = "TEXT"), columns = c(sex = "full"))
profile_compare(p, s)
#>    column      property distance threshold   pass
#>    <char>        <char>    <num>     <num> <lgcl>
#> 1:    sex missing_share     0.00   0.05000   TRUE
#> 2:    sex        levels     0.02   0.08205   TRUE
